claims.claim: Expectancy and placebo-related mechanisms can produce measurable physiological and subjective responses.
claims.correction: Say: "Placebo-related learning, expectation, and treatment context can alter subjective symptoms; some experimental studies also show measurable physiological changes, but effects vary by mechanism and outcome."

citations.author: Goebel et al.
citations.finding_supported: In a double-blind human conditioning experiment, re-exposure to a conditioned cue with placebo capsules suppressed immune measures including IL-2 and IFN-gamma-related outcomes.

citations.author: Benedetti et al.
citations.finding_supported: Among experimental-pain open-label-placebo responders, hidden naloxone reversed analgesia versus saline, consistent with endogenous-opioid involvement.

counterevidence.author: Kleine-Borgmann et al.
counterevidence.finding_supported: Meta-analysis of non-clinical experimental OLP studies found an effect for self-reported outcomes but not overall for objective outcomes.

counterevidence.author: Hróbjartsson and Gøtzsche
counterevidence.finding_supported: Cochrane review concluded placebo interventions generally lacked important clinical effects, while possible benefits were more evident for patient-reported outcomes such as pain.

claims.claim: Open-label placebo has been studied as a treatment approach for chronic low back pain.
claims.correction: Say: "A 2016 randomized trial tested open-label placebo pills added to treatment as usual for chronic low back pain; it found greater short-term self-reported pain and disability improvement than treatment as usual alone."

citations.author: Carvalho et al.
citations.finding_supported: Randomized 97 adults with persistent low back pain; 83 completed. Over 3 weeks, OLP plus treatment as usual produced greater reductions in self-reported pain and Roland-Morris disability than treatment as usual.

citations.author: Locher et al.
citations.finding_supported: A separate chronic-back-pain RCT found lower pain and patient-reported disability with OLP versus usual care, but no effect on objective spine-mobility measures.

counterevidence.author: Carvalho et al.
counterevidence.finding_supported: The comparator was treatment as usual, not a blinded placebo or matched-attention control; the outcomes were self-reported pain and disability.

counterevidence.author: Carvalho et al.
counterevidence.finding_supported: The five-year follow-up reported persistent improvements among recontacted participants but explicitly lacked controls for spontaneous improvement and new cointerventions.

claims.claim: Some open-label placebo effects may occur without deception or a conventional belief that the pill contains active medicine.
claims.correction: Say: "Open-label placebo effects have been observed after participants were told the treatment was a placebo; that does not establish that expectation, belief, learning, rationale, or adherence are irrelevant."

citations.author: Carvalho et al.
citations.finding_supported: Participants knowingly received open-label placebo pills, presented in a positive context, alongside usual treatment.

citations.author: Locher et al.
citations.finding_supported: In an experimental OLP study, positive expectancies and adherence independently predicted most well-being and symptom outcomes.

citations.author: Leibowitz et al.
citations.finding_supported: In an induced-allergic-reaction experiment, placebo belief moderated physiological response in the full OLP condition that combined relationship, ritual, positive expectations, and rationale.

counterevidence.author: Albring et al.
counterevidence.finding_supported: Conditioned immunosuppression altered IL-2 production after repeated cue re-exposure, whereas verbally induced expectation alone did not produce immunosuppression in that experiment.

claims.claim: Copables is a company that mails inert pills to customers.
claims.correction: Say: "Copables markets a 14-day IBS protocol that its own website describes as an open-label-placebo gummy plus app-guided ritual, CBT audio, and written reflection. Its current shipping practices and ingredient-level inertness require verification from product, checkout, and terms materials."

citations.author: Copables
citations.finding_supported: Company page describes a 14-day IBS protocol with a daily OLP gummy, app-guided ritual, digital behavioral therapy, and written field notes; it says "No chemicals."

citations.author: Copables
citations.finding_supported: Company science page says its protocol combines a placebo with a handwritten daily card and presents the offering as based on OLP research.

counterevidence.author: Copables
counterevidence.finding_supported: The page itself describes multiple components beyond a pill/gummy, so attributing any result solely to an inert pill would be unsupported.

claims.claim: A digital intervention might reproduce some therapeutic components of a placebo ritual without a physical pill.
claims.correction: Say: "A digital intervention could deliver some contextual components—timing, instructions, repetition, expectancy framing, and self-monitoring—but equivalence to a physical open-label placebo has not been established."

citations.author: Kaptchuk et al.
citations.finding_supported: An IBS trial experimentally separated observation, placebo-treatment ritual, and an augmented patient-practitioner relationship, supporting the idea that treatment context has separable components.

citations.author: Kleine-Borgmann et al.
citations.finding_supported: An OLP study used a smartphone app to deliver relaxation-practice instructions and evaluation, but the OLP condition still involved a physical placebo intervention.

citations.author: Torous et al.
citations.finding_supported: A randomized study tested expectancy induction around a smartphone-based digital placebo mental-health intervention; participants were debriefed that the intervention had been placebo-oriented.

counterevidence.author: Kleine-Borgmann et al.
counterevidence.finding_supported: The experimental OLP evidence base showed benefits chiefly for self-reported outcomes and no pooled effect for objective outcomes; this does not validate a phone-only clinical substitute.

claims.claim: Ted Kaptchuk is associated with the Program in Placebo Studies and the Therapeutic Encounter at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center and Harvard Medical School.
claims.correction: Say: "Ted J. Kaptchuk is a Harvard Medical School professor and director of the Harvard-wide Program in Placebo Studies and the Therapeutic Encounter (PiPS) at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center."

citations.author: Harvard Medical School, Department of Global Health and Social Medicine
citations.finding_supported: Official profile identifies Kaptchuk as Professor of Medicine and director of the Harvard-wide PiPS at BIDMC.

citations.author: Program in Placebo Studies and the Therapeutic Encounter
citations.finding_supported: Program page identifies PiPS as hosted at BIDMC/Harvard Medical School.

strongest_evidence.author: Carvalho et al.
strongest_evidence.finding_supported: Primary randomized chronic-low-back-pain OLP trial with sample, comparator, outcomes, and effect estimates.

strongest_evidence.author: von Wernsdorff et al.
strongest_evidence.finding_supported: Clinical OLP meta-analysis found a pooled effect versus no treatment, while rating risk of bias as moderate and the field as early-stage.

strongest_evidence.author: Goebel et al.
strongest_evidence.finding_supported: Primary human evidence that conditioning associated with placebo administration can alter laboratory immune outcomes.

counterevidence.author: Kleine-Borgmann et al.
counterevidence.finding_supported: No overall effect of OLPs on objective outcomes in a meta-analysis of experimental non-clinical studies.

counterevidence.author: Locher et al.
counterevidence.finding_supported: OLP improved self-reported chronic-back-pain measures but not objective spine mobility.

counterevidence.author: Albring et al.
counterevidence.finding_supported: Verbal expectation alone did not induce conditioned immunosuppression in the reported experiment.

open_questions.question: Does Copables currently mail the gummies, and what are their complete ingredients?
Are Copables' IBS outcome claims based on Copables-run clinical research, or are they extrapolated from third-party OLP trials?
Has any trial directly compared a pill-based OLP ritual with a phone-only, transparent digital placebo ritual for the same condition and outcome?
Which digital components are hypothesized to be active: expectancy script, reminder schedule, self-monitoring, CBT content, clinician contact, or physical ritual?

sources_to_verify.verification_needed: Current checkout/shipping coverage, full ingredient list, product labeling, whether gummies are pharmacologically inert, and any efficacy disclaimers.
Underlying references for claims that belief does not predict outcome and that its protocol has specified neurological effects.
Full-text protocol details: exact OLP explanatory script, pill composition, contact-time balance, adherence measurement, and prespecified versus exploratory outcomes.
